findings.claim: FC-R06 / ERP_RIDER_SHARE give RydeFLASH the full share 1.0 whenever the carpool status is not recorded, although Ryde's own article ties RydeFLASH to carpool drivers, for whom the rider owes only 50%. The ontology declares is_carpool a data gap (absent from the organizer record), so the default applies to every RydeFLASH case. The missing exception is silent: nothing sends an unrecorded carpool status for this service to FC-R12 or GEN-R07, unlike an unrecorded service type.
findings.evidence: 33363192453785: 'RydeFLASH (Up to 4 pax)** Available to Carpool, Private Hire and Taxi drivers'; 360003567993: '* A 10% service fee applies to Carpool Drivers'; ontology.yaml line 102: '{name: is_carpool, type: boolean, data_gap: true ...'; engine_toll.py line 50: 'carpool = code == "CARPOOL" or trip.get("is_carpool") is True'. Probe: RydeFLASH, gantries S$2.50 + S$4.00, no is_carpool, S$6.50 charged -> UPHOLD, amount 0.0, tier AUTO, reasons ['FC-R-TOLL-VALID'].
findings.failure_scenario: A RydeFLASH trip served by a carpool driver, case record without is_carpool, rider charged the full S$6.50 ERP. If the trip is a carpool trip the rider owes S$3.25, so the right result is TOLL_REFUND S$3.25 with a driver fraud signal at APPROVE; the KB upholds the charge at AUTO. It would be CRITICAL for every RydeFLASH carpool trip if the case data never carries the flag (the ontology says it does not).
findings.suggested_fix: In FC-R06, the ontology note and rider_share(): for RYDEFLASH (the one service the corpus ties to carpool drivers) a carpool status that is not recorded (is_carpool absent or None) is insufficient data (FC-R12, RECORDS_MISSING) or GEN-R07, not share 1.0; only an explicit is_carpool False gives 1.0. Add a test and note it in D35.

findings.claim: The rule card and the engine disagree on a carpool-flagged trip of a service that has no share. FC-R06 says Ryde sets no share for RydePOOL, RydeHIRE, Ryde X GO and Ryde+ (GEN-R07, tier HUMAN) and names only RydeSEND+carpool as undefined; the ontology note names only RYDESEND too. rider_share() applies 0.5 to any service except RydeSEND when is_carpool is True, so those services get a ruling, a refund and a driver FRAUD_SIGNAL at tier APPROVE and the RydePOOL source conflict is resolved silently (META-04 forbids that). T05 even expects RydeX+carpool to be 0.5, while Ryde's article says RydeX is 'No sharing'.
findings.evidence: rules.yaml FC-R06: 'Ryde's articles set no share for any other service (RydePOOL, whose 2026 and 2023 driver pages disagree, RydeHIRE, Ryde X GO, Ryde+) and none for a trip that is both RydeSEND and carpool: no rule covers it and GEN-R07 applies.' Engine: 'if carpool: return {"share": float(table["CARPOOL"]), ...}' after only the RYDESEND check. Probe (S$2.50 + S$4.00 gantries, S$6.50 charged, is_carpool True): RydePOOL, RydeHIRE, Ryde X GO, Other and RydeTAXI all give TOLL_REFUND 3.25, fraud ['DRIVER'], tier APPROVE, reasons ['FC-R-TOLL-OVERSTATED'], where the card says ESCALATE_HUMAN / HUMAN / GEN-R-POLICY-GAP. 33363192453785: 'RydeX (up to 4 pax)** Private Hire Bookings. ... No sharing.'
findings.failure_scenario: A RydeHIRE trip (2023 pages: fares include ERP, share 0) or RydePOOL trip (sources conflict) with is_carpool true and the full ERP charged: the KB proposes a S$3.25 refund and marks the driver as having overstated ERP, instead of sending the share question to a person. A driver who charged what Ryde's other page allows gets a fraud signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide and write it in FC-R06 and the ontology note: either a carpool flag on a service with no share goes to GEN-R07 (change rider_share() so only services with a share row, or CARPOOL itself, take 0.5; add tests for RydePOOL/RydeHIRE/Ryde X GO/Ryde+/Other with is_carpool True), or state in the card that the carpool exception overrides the service list and drop the claim that those services have no share. findings.claim: FC-R08 says FC-R07's refund and FC-R08's refund 'together refund at most the ERP charged minus ERP(recommended)', which is false when the recommended route carries more ERP than the actual path. findings.evidence: FC-R08: 'FC-R07's refund of an overstated ERP line comes on top, so together they refund at most the ERP charged minus ERP(recommended), never a negative amount.' findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the sentence in en and zh: the ceiling holds when ERP(recommended) is at most ERP(actual); otherwise FC-R07 refunds the whole overstatement (charged minus ERP(actual)) and FC-R08 refunds nothing. Add a test.

findings.claim: The FC-R07 zh text and the English differ at the tolerance boundary. English refunds when the ERP charged exceeds the expected ERP 'by more than' TOLL_TOLERANCE_SGD (strict, as the engine does); zh says 'exceeds ... 达 TOLL_TOLERANCE_SGD 以上', which means by that amount or more. The tolerance has a plausible range up to S$0.50, so the two texts give different answers when the excess equals the tolerance.
findings.evidence: EN: 'exceeds F-ERP-EXPECTED (...) by more than TOLL_TOLERANCE_SGD, refund the difference'; ZH: '实收乘客的 ERP 超过 F-ERP-EXPECTED（...）达 TOLL_TOLERANCE_SGD 以上，退差额'; reference_data TOLL_TOLERANCE_SGD plausible_range [0.00, 0.50]; engine: 'charged - actual > tol + 1e-9'.
findings.failure_scenario: With the tolerance at S$0.50 and an ERP line exactly S$0.50 over, the English and the engine do not refund, the zh text does.
findings.suggested_fix: Change zh to '超过 ... 且超出部分大于 TOLL_TOLERANCE_SGD' (strictly greater).

findings.claim: The record of why Ryde X GO, Ryde+ (and RydeHIRE) have no share is one-sided. ADVERSARIAL TEST OF THE CHANGED LOGIC (e.dimension: ADVERSARIAL TEST OF THE CHANGED LOGIC (engine_toll.py, engine_gates.py, FC-R06/F04/R07/R08/F03/R01, AUTH-04, and the D34 item 1 change in engine_noshow.py)
checked_ok: Ran about 170 new ERP edge cases through T.run (scripts in /tmp/a2check2/erp_adv.py, codes.py, prop.py), 29 through T.fc_r01 (r01_g3_adv.py), 24 through G.resolve_g3, and 99 variants x flagged/unflagged rider through E.run (g3_pairs.py). The repo was not modified (git status clean after rerun_engine.py wrote to /tmp).
Baseline: python3 kb/tools/selftest.py passes (99/99 variants, 561/561 readings, 27 ERP cases). rerun_engine.py E01 E02 E03 E04 E11 gives 5/5, E11 TOLL_REFUND S$6.00 at APPROVE.

Every TX-SERVICE code with is_carpool None and True, plus the spelling variants 'ryde-send', 'RYDE SEND', 'Ryde_Send', ' RydeSEND ', 'Ryde X GO', 'ryde-x-go', 'RydeX' with a zero-width space: share and gap are as FC-R06 says (RydePOOL, RydeHIRE, Ryde X GO, Ryde+ and OTHER without carpool flag -> GEN-R07 at HUMAN; UNKNOWN/None/blank/7 -> FC-R12 at HUMAN; RydeSEND+carpool -> GEN-R07). The unrecognized strings 'Send', 'Delivery', 'Pool', 'Taxi', 'RydeX (carpool)' fail safe to FC-R12 at HUMAN.

Refund arithmetic: in 60,000 random cases (6 services, random actual and recommended gantry sets, random charged amounts) the refund never exceeded the ERP charged, was never negative, was never at tier AUTO, and the rider was never left paying less than min(ERP(actual), ERP(recommended)). Charged at, just above, below ERP(recommended) and ERP(actual), carpool halves, RydeSEND, exact S$10.00 limit and S$10.01 all behave as FC-R07/FC-R08 state (D04, D05, D06, D18, D19, D20). Only the 'at most charged minus ERP(recommended)' sentence of FC-R08 fails (finding A2R2-04).

Tier logic of engine_toll.run: every TOLL_REFUND is APPROVE (a fraud trigger or decisive FC-F03 always fires), every ESCALATE_HUMAN is HUMAN, UPHOLD at AUTO only arises with no overcharge, no potential detour refund, no tolerance sensitivity. Justification variants ('', ' ', 'none', 'no', 'false', 'N/A', 'driver says GPS', False, 0, []) can never produce AUTO when a detour could change the amount: a truthy justification gives UPHOLD at APPROVE (decisive FC-F03). Metered detour with and without justification, with charged equal to ERP(recommended), with an FC-R07 overstatement (T01, T02, T07, T08, T10) behave as D32 and T27 state.

Tolerance edges and rounding: charged 2.504 -> valid, 2.505 -> S$0.01 refund with fraud signal (tol 0.00 by design, flagged decisive); with TOLL_TOLERANCE_SGD moved to 0.30 (in-memory copy) over 0.30 -> UPHOLD at APPROVE (decisive), over 0.31 -> refund 0.31; carpool 1.125 and 1.375 expected values round half up and do not misfire (R04 to R08).

Gate G3 (engine_gates.resolve_g3): blind WAIVE_FEE/UPHOLD/TOLL_REFUND at AUTO with a differing aware pass -> APPROVE with the blind outcome and amount unchanged; blind ESCALATE_HUMAN or outcome None -> HUMAN; blind tier HUMAN (for example G4) is never lowered (max); fraud_check_disagrees alone fires G3; no disagreement leaves the tier untouched. Across all 99 variants a flagged and an unflagged rider got identical outcomes and amounts, and the flagged rider's tier was never lower and never AUTO (FX5 holds beyond the 2 pairs in g3_check).

findings.claim: is_metered tests 'metered' as a substring of fare_type, so 'Non-metered', 'unmetered' and 'fixed (not metered)' count as METERED. findings.claim: Two trace and evidence gaps: (a) when an FC-R07 overstatement was found and the recommended route's rate is then unknown, the run ends ESCALATE_HUMAN with reasons ['FC-R-TOLL-OVERSTATED', 'FC-R-INSUFFICIENT-DATA'] and the DRIVER fraud signal kept, although FC-R12 says to make no adverse finding when escalating, and erp_code_check's own rule (a reason carries its outcome) is violated; the metered branch resets reasons but this branch does not; (b) identical duplicate rows in gantry_passes are counted as two passes.

findings.claim: fc_r01 decides 'extra gantries' by gantry name only, while run() decides by rate and activity, so FC-R01 can fail to open the FC-TOLL claim that FC-R08 would pay, or open a pointless one. Also the gantry rate fallback ignores the UTC offset of the timestamp.
findings.evidence: Same gantry name on both paths with different rates (actual 'CTE (southbound)' 6.00 at a higher band, recommended 2.50): fc_r01 -> extra [] and toll_claim None, while T.run gives TOLL_REFUND 3.50. Recommended lists the extra gantry as inactive: extra [] (run: 4.00 refund). A spelling difference ('cte (southbound)') opens a claim for a gantry both routes pass (UPHOLD AUTO, harmless). gantry_rate slices timestamp[11:16]: '2026-09-09T08:40:00Z' (16:40 in Singapore) is banded as 08:40 and gets 6.00 -> UPHOLD AUTO.
findings.failure_scenario: A longer route that moves the pass of the same gantry into a dearer time band is not sent to FC-TOLL; a UTC log time picks the wrong band when the log carries no rate.
findings.suggested_fix: Open the claim when ERP(actual) > ERP(recommended) computed as run() does (names only as a pre-filter), and parse the timestamp with its offset into Asia/Singapore before reading HH:MM.

findings.claim: FC-R07 puts the FRAUD_SIGNAL on the driver for any ERP line above expected without checking who entered it. The E11 case carries erp_toll_source ('keyed in by driver at drop-off') and the engine ignores it; an empty gantry log with an ERP line charged also yields refund plus a driver fraud signal without checking that a GPS trace exists to support 'no gantry passed'.
findings.evidence: Code reads only fare_breakdown.erp_toll and erp_charges.gantry_passes. mk(gantries=(), charged=2.50) -> TOLL_REFUND 2.50 FRAUD_SIGNAL DRIVER at APPROVE (M01); RydeSEND with any ERP line -> driver fraud signal whatever the source field says. findings.failure_scenario: A RydeSEND ERP line added by the platform's fare calculation (erp_toll_source 'system') is booked as a fraud signal against the driver; or a trip with a missing GPS trace and an empty gantry list flags the driver.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise the driver signal only when erp_toll_source says the driver keyed it (otherwise refund and flag a platform error), and send an empty gantry list with no usable GPS trace to FC-R12. Note both in FC-R07.

findings.claim: resolve_g3 does not validate its inputs: a blind tier with a stray character or other case ('HUMAN ', 'human') counts as the lowest and is downgraded to APPROVE; an outcome 'escalate_human' in lower case is not recognized as ESCALATE_HUMAN (tier APPROVE instead of HUMAN); a blind ruling without a 'tier' key raises KeyError.
findings.evidence: G.resolve_g3(kb, {'outcome':'UPHOLD','amount':None,'tier':'HUMAN '}, {'outcome':'WAIVE_FEE','amount':None}) -> tier APPROVE; {'outcome':'escalate_human','tier':'AUTO'} fired -> tier APPROVE; blind without 'tier' -> KeyError 'tier'. findings.failure_scenario: A mis-typed tier string from the caller turns a HUMAN case into APPROVE. The code comment says an unknown tier counts as lowest on purpose, which is the unsafe side for a malformed HUMAN.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize with str(x).strip().upper(), treat an unknown tier as HUMAN (fail safe) and an unknown or missing outcome as ESCALATE_HUMAN.

findings.claim: AUTH-04's tie-break 'If one disagreement fits both G3 and G8 ..., G3 applies' can be read as letting G3 absorb a separate G8 disagreement: the history-blind pass against the rules engine. When the history-blind pass and the rules engine (both history-free) disagree and the history-aware pass sides with the engine, the blind ruling becomes the provisional ruling at APPROVE although it is the outlier. engine_gates has no G8 input, so the code cannot show which is meant.
findings.evidence: Text: 'G8 the Judge passes disagree with each other or with the rules engine' and 'If one disagreement fits both G3 and G8 (the history-aware pass is a Judge pass), G3 applies.' Three-way case: blind = X, aware = Y, engine = Y. The blind-versus-engine disagreement is a G8 only; blind-versus-aware fits both.
findings.failure_scenario: An LLM reviewer applies 'G3 applies' to the whole case and keeps the minority blind ruling at APPROVE; before A2 this was HUMAN under G8.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'The tie-break covers only the disagreement between the history-aware and the history-blind pass; a disagreement between the history-blind pass and the rules engine (or between two history-free passes) stays G8 (HUMAN).' Optionally give resolve_g3 an engine ruling argument.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced with a scratch probe under /tmp/a2check2: RydeFLASH, gantries S$2.50+S$4.00, no is_carpool, S$6.50 charged gives UPHOLD 0.0, tier AUTO, FC-R-TOLL-VALID. The same case with is_carpool True gives TOLL_REFUND 3.25 at APPROVE with a driver fraud signal. Read the sources myself. Article 33363192453785 says 'RydeFLASH ... Available to Carpool, Private Hire and Taxi drivers'. Other corpus articles treat Carpool Drivers as a driver category (360003567993 '10% service fee applies to Carpool Drivers'; 46374495669401 and 46489492021401 on cost recovery under the Car Pools Exemption Order). So 'carpool trip' plausibly means a trip by a carpool driver, and a RydeFLASH trip can be one. The RydePET and RydeX articles name private-hire and taxi drivers only, so FLASH is the one service the corpus ties to carpool drivers. ontology.yaml line 102 marks is_carpool data_gap true. Neither FC-R06, FC-F04 nor the ontology says how an unrecorded carpool status is read (the silent default is 'not carpool'), yet PB-FC-TOLL required_evidence lists 'whether the trip is a carpool trip (is_carpool)'. engine_toll.rider_share only escalates an unrecorded service type, not an unrecorded carpool status. Severity: MAJOR is right, not CRITICAL. DISP-002 records no service type (taxonomy TX-SERVICE UNKNOWN), so organizer-format cases already escalate under FC-R12. The failure needs a case that carries service_type RydeFLASH but no carpool flag, and carpool trips with several riders are in the scope.yaml backlog. The remedy (escalate versus default to non-carpool, and whether to add an organizer question) is the owner's decision; at minimum the default must be written in FC-R06 and the ontology.

Reproduced the engine behavior (is_carpool True with RydePOOL, RydeHIRE, Ryde X GO, Other, RydeTAXI and RydeX all give TOLL_REFUND 3.25, fraud DRIVER, tier APPROVE; Ryde+ is not recognized, see G9). But 'card and engine disagree' depends on how FC-R06 is read. The card gives '0.5 for a carpool trip' as a trip-level share and names only RydeSEND+carpool as undefined. The ontology note for is_carpool says the same ('Together with RYDESEND the share is undefined'). FC-F04 lists 'another service, or RydeSEND and carpool at once' as the no-share cases, and the playbook lists carpool 0.5 before the services. The engine follows the ontology and T05, so the card's wording is ambiguous (MINOR: say whether the carpool share overrides a no-share service). The reviewer's T05 point is a misreading: article 33363192453785 puts the 'For Carpool trips: ... 50%' paragraph under the RydeX heading itself, and 'No sharing' there is about sharing the ride, not about ERP. One piece has weight. For RydePOOL with is_carpool True the engine silently takes 0.5, while RydePOOL without the flag goes to GEN-R07 because of the 2023 versus 2026 page conflict that META-04 says must be surfaced (SOURCE_CONFLICT). That path is APPROVE with a human deciding the fraud consequence, never AUTO. RydePOOL is backlog-scope, so the impact is small. The owner should state the intended order; I do not rate it MAJOR.

Reproduced. It fails only when the avoided-gantry path is cheaper in ERP than the recommended one and the line is overstated. That is a corner case, the refund is at tier APPROVE, and the formula and FC-R07 are explicit. So it is a wrong gloss to reword, not a MAJOR.
